label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_wall_heraldry

surfaces.part: ashlar wall face with stone courses
light merlon-like cornice strip at the wall's upper edge
iron rods holding the banners
left and right blue banners hung flat
blue and gold shield
string-course ledge near the bottom

answer.evidence: The drawing is a flat, face-on stretch of wall, 64 px wide and 96 rows tall. The banners, shield and rods are all drawn as flat vertical faces, with no receding top or side. The rods at rows 33-34 are thin strips with no top surface. The pale cornice strip at rows 22-30 has an edge line at row 31 but no real depth or shadow. The ledge at rows 84-85 is a 1-2 row lip. There is no ellipse, roof or contents. The whole piece is a front elevation, which is acceptable for a flat wall-mounted item.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, inside the reference range (hedge 9, cheese stall 17, roofed well 20) and well above the bench and lamp, which are too thin to measure. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The ashlar wall has individually shaded stones in about 5 grey steps, with speckle, mortar lines, a crenellated cap and grass tufts at the base, which matches the per-stone shading and grain in the references. The banners and shield are small, with only about 3-4 blue and gold steps and fairly dark edges. 46% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, which fits the bench (44%) and roofed well (33%), so I call the outline mixed. It reads as tinted stone-toned shading rather than a uniform black sticker line. Density and craft sit at the references' level, so a careful artist would accept it next to them.
